candidates.summary: A func literal's params and results are masked before their types are walked, so a type that reads an enclosing loop var binds to the wrong variable
candidates.failure_scenario: `x := [3]int{}; for x := [2]int{}; x[0] < 1; x[0]++ { f := func() (x [len(x)]int) { return }; println(len(f())) }` prints 3 under gno and 2 under Go, with no error: the result type resolves to the outer [3]int. The param form `func(x [len(x)]int)` is refused with `name x not declared`. initStaticBlocks1 still masks FuncLit params and results at TRANS_ENTER, before TRANS_FUNCLIT_TYPE is walked, though Go resolves those types in the enclosing scope. This is the scope-timing mistake the PR fixes for range X and type-switch X, left in the same function. It predates the diff, and it is in scope because the diff sweeps this class here and misses this member.

candidates.evidence: head 1de7f587d: `Output diff: -2 +3` (Go `go run`: 2). Merge base (preprocess.go+transcribe.go reverted in scratch): same `-2 +3`, so it predates the diff. Param variant at head and base: `zz_solo2_paramlen.gno:5:20-21: name x not declared`; the control without a loop passes. With the FuncLitExpr pushClone moved from TRANS_ENTER to TRANS_BLOCK (the patch), both pass, and the 372 TestFiles matching loopvar|closure|heap|range|for|switch|typeswitch|fun|var|block|shadow stay green, except switch13.gno, which also fails unpatched on the local Go 1.27 toolchain (go/types message text). The miscompile is on master. It fires only where the realm's own source has this shape, and nothing outside can induce it, so it is treated here as ordinary review output in the PR's swept class.

candidates.summary: A program master accepts changes output: a for-init that reads a plain shadow of an outer loop var printed the wrong values on master and prints Go's under this PR
candidates.failure_scenario: `for x := 0; x < 1; x++ { x := 5; for x := x; x < 7; x++ { println(x) } }` runs on master and prints 0 1 2 3 4 5 6, because the inner init RHS was renamed to the outer loop's x.loopvar. At head it prints 5 6, matching Go. The ADR says its regression files each failed before with an error, and it calls the nested case's AST unchanged. Neither says that an accepted program's output and executed work change. Initialize re-preprocesses every stored package (gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:203), so a deployed realm with this shape computes differently once a node runs this binary: a consensus-visible change on upgrade that the PR does not name. The shape is already public in the PR's own loopvar_shadow_init_capture_3.gno (shadowBetween).
